title: Tiered Recursive-Descent Expression Parser
description: Encode operator precedence and left-associativity through the call hierarchy parse_expr -> parse_addsub -> parse_muldiv -> parse_unary -> parse_primary.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Tokenize the input with tokenize(src) and define Parser with peek(), advance(), and expect(ttype).
In parse_addsub and parse_muldiv, parse the tighter tier first, then loop with while self.peek() to fold any chain of '+'/'-' or '*'/'/' operators into left-leaning (op, node, rhs) tuples.
In parse_unary, consume a leading '-' and recurse into parse_unary(); in parse_primary, match either a 'NUM' token or '(' followed by self.parse_expr() and ')'.

steps.question: Why does calling self.parse_expr() inside the 'LPAREN' branch on line 79 allow '(2+3)*4' to group '+' inside '*'?
steps.answer: When parse_muldiv calls parse_unary -> parse_primary on '(2+3)', line 79 restarts at the top of the hierarchy (parse_expr -> parse_addsub). It resolves ('+', 2.0, 3.0) as a single primary node before returning to parse_muldiv for '* 4'.

steps.description: Wrap Parser(src).parse_expr() in parse(src) and print the resulting AST tuples for six test expressions.
Watch parse_primary consume the first number token ('NUM', '2') and return ('num', 2.0) up the call chain.
